  • Caxcan↗Historical regional connection in specialist scholarship
    Connection & source
    Historical regional connection in specialist scholarship

    The opening abstract explicitly places Caxcan communities in the south of present-day Zacatecas and the northwestern Los Altos area of Jalisco at Spanish arrival. This directly supports Mexico as a historical country-level index. Inspection: Actual PDF downloaded normally with valid TLS, HTTP 200; 27 pages available. Spanish and English introductory abstracts, printed pp.158–159 / PDF pp.1–2, inspected. No burial-site details, images or coordinates are used. Limits: Contemporary communities and recognition are not established by this historical abstract. Only country-level navigation is proposed, not an exclusive territory.

    Early sixteenth century, including the period of Spanish arrival in 1531. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Coahuiltecan↗Historical regional umbrella in specialist reference
    Connection & source
    Historical regional umbrella in specialist reference

    Actual introductory and geographic sections place this broad historical label in southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. The article emphasizes many autonomous named groups and uncertain classification. This route does not assert one unified people/government, adopt extinction claims or establish modern recognition.

    Historical geography described in Handbook of Texas; inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Coca↗Specific community geography in a community authored published chapter
    Connection & source
    Specific community geography in a community authored published chapter

    The government-published volume identifies Mezcala, Jalisco in its title. Rocío Moreno, introduced as a Mezcala comunera and Coca delegate, explicitly identifies Mezcala as a Coca Indigenous community on the north side of Lake Chapala. This supports a Mexico connection through one identified community.

    Mezcala community described in a 2017 publication. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Cochimí↗Historical peninsula connection with identity scope caveat
    Connection & source
    Historical peninsula connection with identity scope caveat

    The government cultural record explicitly associates Cochimí history with the Baja California peninsula and lists Baja California in its distribution field. This supports a broad Mexico route. The narrower implications of the identity label remain unresolved. Inspection: Actual HTML geographic distribution and opening mission-history paragraphs, plus modification credit inspected (current extraction lines 264–287 and 308–311). Limits: The record juxtaposes historical Cochimí, Tipai identification at La Huerta and San Antonio Nécua, and descendants at Santa Gertrudis; these are not treated as automatically interchangeable. No demographic count, extinction assertion, current leadership or language classification is adopted. Country-level geography is supported; a more precise community/period account needs later review.

    Mission-era Baja California history, in a government record last modified 2019. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

  • Mactun↗Historical Acalán/Mactun name connection in specialist scholarship
    Connection & source
    Historical Acalán/Mactun name connection in specialist scholarship

    Voss explicitly uses Acalan (Mactun) for a place of origin in southern Campeche in his discussion of merchants and colonial accounts. This supports a Mexico route for the directory’s historical-name access point. It does not establish a separate present-day nation called Mactun. Inspection: Actual publicly displayed full article text, printed pp.257–258, especially the paragraph at p.258 / web lines 1649–1671. Title, author, DOI and public-full-text/license context were also inspected; the complete 61-page work was not read. Limits: Only the historical name/location correspondence is used. The underlying Cortés edition was not independently read. This passage does not establish a present political organization, citizenship category or equivalence with all Chontal/Yokot’an people. The UNAM book’s reported amactún / mactún uinicob self-designations remain a separate original-source check.

    Late Postclassic / sixteenth-century setting discussed in a 2018 article. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
